newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up at close on inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up at close on inflation data.

text.p: Mexican stocks rebounded to close slightly firmer Thursday after a late spurt sparked by surprisingly mild inflation figures.
But the session was dull as the market awaited the government's 1997 budget proposals, which turned out much as expected.
"Inflation figures nudged the Bolsa up towards the close," a trader at the Bancomer brokerage said.
The blue chip IPC index ended up 2.85 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2,293.23 on light volume of 49.8 million shares.

Banco de Mexico announced late Thursday that consumer inflation for October was 1.25 percent, slightly below average expectations of 1.31 percent and the lowest monthly figure since the December 1994 peso crisis.

"Budget guidelines were as expected, especially the forecast average exchange rate, which had caused some jitters," said another trader. The government expects the peso exchange rate to average 8.53 per dollar next year.
On the broad market, a total of 106 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered winners by a margin of 50 to 33.

The losers list was dominated by three series of shares in financial firm GFInver. The ACP series fell most, by 11 centavos (1 cent) to 55 centavos (7 cents). Traders said this was due to speculation ahead of an announcement of the subscription price for new shares to be issued to help finance the banking subsidiary's forthcoming acquisition by Banco Santander.
Holding company Gruma topped the leaders, closing up 2.10 pesos (27 cents) at 42.70 ($5.39). Traders noted that Gruma recently placed $120 million of stock.
Traders felt that budget proposals could ease uncertainty and pave the way for gains on Friday.
"We could see a market with brighter prospects and livelier volume tomorrow, now that the uncertainty over budget proposals is behind us," the Bancomer trader said.
